name: Glomerulus
summary: Where the nephron starts: plasma is filtered from the glomerular capillaries into Bowman’s space through a barrier of fenestrated endothelium, basement membrane and podocytes. Water and small solutes (Na⁺, glucose, urea, amino acids) pass freely; albumin and cells are held back by size and negative charge. GFR (~120 mL/min) depends on Starling forces and the tone of the afferent (prostaglandins dilate; NSAIDs) and efferent (angiotensin II constricts; ACE inhibitors) arterioles. Nephrotic syndrome: protein leaks; nephritic syndrome: blood and inflammation.

alb_l.name: Albumin (Bowman’s space)
alb_l.notes: Normally almost none: albumin in the urine (>30 mg/day) is an early sign of diabetic nephropathy; heavy proteinuria is nephrotic syndrome.

rbc_l.name: Red blood cells (Bowman’s space)
rbc_l.notes: Normally none. Dysmorphic red cells and RBC casts mean glomerular bleeding: nephritic syndrome.

filt.name: Ultrafiltration (Starling forces)
filt.notes: Glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure pushes plasma water and small solutes out, against the pressure in Bowman’s space and the plasma oncotic pressure. GFR is about 120 mL/min (inulin clearance; creatinine clearance estimates it). Constricting the efferent arteriole (angiotensin II) raises GFR; ACE inhibitors and ARBs lower it. Dilating the afferent arteriole (prostaglandins) raises it; NSAIDs lower it. Filtration fraction = GFR / RPF, about 20%.

barrier.name: Filtration barrier (size and charge)
barrier.notes: Fenestrated endothelium, the glomerular basement membrane (negatively charged heparan sulfate) and podocyte foot processes with slit diaphragms (nephrin). Albumin is held back by its size and negative charge. Nephrotic syndrome: the barrier (often the podocytes) fails, more than 3.5 g/day of protein. Nephritic syndrome: inflammation breaks it, letting red cells through (hematuria, RBC casts).
